title: Machine Learning
description: Understand machine-learning concepts, build and evaluate a baseline model, and prepare models for responsible deployment.

paths.title: Machine Learning Foundations
paths.description: Understand features, labels, training, prediction, and problem types.

paths.title: Train and Evaluate a Model
paths.description: Split data, build a baseline, evaluate metrics, and avoid leakage.

paths.title: Responsible Machine Learning
paths.description: Consider drift, fairness, explainability, and deployment risk.

cards.title: Machine learning learns patterns from examples
cards.prompt: A machine-learning model maps inputs to outputs using parameters estimated from data.
cards.content: Use machine learning when rules are difficult to write explicitly and enough representative data exists. Simpler rules are often better for stable, transparent logic.

cards.title: Features are inputs; labels are targets
cards.prompt: Supervised learning uses example features paired with known labels.
cards.content: At prediction time, every required feature must be available before the outcome occurs. Otherwise the model may rely on leakage.

options: Predict whether an email is spam
question.explanation: Spam detection predicts a category, while the other examples predict numeric values.

cards.title: Training fits parameters; inference uses them
cards.prompt: Training searches for model parameters that reduce an objective on examples. Inference applies the fitted model to new inputs.
cards.content: Keep training and serving transformations consistent so the model receives the same feature definitions in both stages.

cards.title: Build a model baseline
cards.prompt: Start with a simple reference before testing complex algorithms.
cards.content: A baseline reveals whether added complexity produces meaningful improvement and catches broken metrics or leakage.
steps: Choose a simple rule or model.

cards.title: Train, validation, and test sets have different roles
cards.prompt: Training data fits parameters, validation data guides choices, and test data estimates final generalization.
cards.content: Repeatedly checking the test set turns it into another validation set and makes the final estimate optimistic.

cards.title: Choose a metric for rare positives
cards.prompt: A fraud dataset has 0.2% positive cases. Why can accuracy be misleading?

options: Predicting no fraud can be highly accurate but useless
question.explanation: A majority-only model can score about 99.8% accuracy while finding no fraud.

cards.title: Create a reproducible classification pipeline
cards.prompt: A pipeline applies preprocessing and the model consistently during fitting and evaluation.
cards.content: The split is stratified so both sets preserve the target proportion. The random state makes the experiment repeatable.

code.snippet:
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression

X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
    X, y, test_size=0.2, stratify=y, random_state=42
)
model = make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), LogisticRegression())
model.fit(X_train, y_train)
print(model.score(X_test, y_test))

cards.title: Model quality can change after deployment
cards.prompt: Data drift, concept drift, upstream schema changes, and feedback loops can reduce performance.
cards.content: Monitor input distributions, missingness, latency, prediction rates, and delayed outcome metrics. A one-time test is not permanent assurance.

cards.title: Fairness depends on context and harm
cards.prompt: Different fairness metrics can conflict, especially when base rates differ across groups.
cards.content: Define affected groups, decisions, false-positive and false-negative costs, legal constraints, and appeal mechanisms before choosing metrics.

cards.title: Use human review appropriately
cards.prompt: When should a high-impact model most strongly include human review and an appeal path?

options: When denying essential benefits or opportunities
question.explanation: High-impact decisions need stronger oversight, explanation, and recourse.

cards.title: Prepare a model for deployment
cards.prompt: Deployment includes the surrounding system, not only a serialized model file.
cards.content: Document intended use and prohibited use so downstream teams understand the model's limits.
items: Version data, code, and model artifacts.
